what_worked: Strong narrative arc with numbered surprises, clear plain-language framing, and effective callback structure between slides.
fix_next: Slide 10 claims top 10% earn 91% and slide 12 uses means not medians; verify statistics against the actual dataset before presenting.
verdict: Well-structured storytelling undermined by several factual inaccuracies and shallow analysis.
factual_error_detail: Slide 10: Claims top 10% earn 91% of revenue; reference shows top-10 share is ~49.6%, so 91% for top 100 is plausible but unverified and the chart's cumulative structure (97%, 99%, 100%…) looks fabricated/inflated. Slide 10: Claims single biggest business earns 23% — unverifiable and suspiciously high. Slide 12: B2B vs B2C comparison uses means ($10,319 vs $2,735) and claims '4×' but reference medians show only ~2.3× difference; presenting means as 'typical' is misleading. Slide 11: Uses mean revenue per country but calls it 'typical' — median would be appropriate given extreme skew acknowledged on slide 10. Slide 9: Says B2C is 56% and 'the biggest group (4 in 10)' — internally contradictory (56% ≠ 4 in 10). Slide 6: Omits that 274 rows lack category data, presenting counts as if they cover all 1,000.

evidence.insight: Slides 10-14 attempt genuine surprises (concentration, dormancy, for-sale pricing). The count-vs-cash framing on slide 11 is a real insight. However, analysis stays at descriptive level — no cross-cuts, no category-revenue median analysis, no discussion of AI's low median despite high total.
evidence.narrative: Clear five-surprise structure with callbacks (slide 7→11, slide 9→12). Summary slide 15 ties it together. The 'crowded doesn't mean profitable' thread is set up on slide 6 but never fully delivered with category median data.
evidence.framing: Slides 1-4 establish context well for a cold reader. However, missing data is never disclosed (241 missing country, 274 missing category, 288 missing audience_type). The claim on slide 4 that 'money numbers are complete for every single business' is true but misleadingly implies all fields are complete.
evidence.accuracy: Slide 10's 91% top-decile claim and 23% single-company claim are unverified against reference. Slide 12 uses means labeled as 'typical' despite acknowledging extreme skew. Slide 9 internal contradiction (56% vs '4 in 10'). Slide 11 uses means for skewed data. Missing-data denominators never addressed for category/country charts.
evidence.visual: Consistent teal color scheme, clean bar charts with direct labels, good use of sidebar callout boxes. Donut chart on slide 9 is acceptable. Slide 10's bar chart is a poor choice for cumulative percentages — a stacked area or Lorenz curve would communicate inequality better. Overall restrained and legible but repetitive template.
evidence.ai_slop: Moderate template repetition (every slide has identical sidebar callout box pattern). The 'everyday analogy' on slide 2 feels like generic AI filler. Overall not severe but the uniform structure across all slides suggests AI-generated template with minimal customization.
